# Tickets images

**Complexity:** 6

## Goal

A ticket inline image must render the first time it is looked at, and survive a refetch. Two plans in two different tickets features. The retry added by the first changes an image height after first paint, which is the moment the markdown editor scroll-sync re-measures, so the two are cross-referenced.

## Dependencies & sequencing (2026-09-04, Board Collapse audit)

Two plans that were in two different tickets features. Both are about an inline image rendering when
it should.

1. **Tickets Panel: Inline Images Are Blank On First View And Only Appear After Clicking Around** —
   the first-view failure and its self-recovery: a one-shot scheme-gated `img` retry, the render-memo
   bypass when the pane holds a proven failure, deferring the remote description until the local read
   lands, and resolving the asset allow-list through the host seam so the browser cockpit gets
   loadable URLs. This is the larger of the two and goes first.
2. **Refetch Leaves Inline Images Blank Until Second Click** — a three-line addition to the
   `importAllTicketsComplete` handler, re-reading the selected ticket's local file after a refetch.
   It relies on the unconditional render in `localTicketFileRead`, which step 1 does not remove.

**Cross-feature coupling, recorded 2026-09-04.** Step 1's retry changes an image's height *after*
first paint. That is exactly the moment the markdown editor's scroll-sync plan
(*The Editor and the Preview Stay Level*) re-measures its anchor map, because an image's height is
unknown until it loads and that is when the editor and preview columns diverge. Whichever lands
second must make the retry trigger the re-measure. Both plans carry this note.

Two other cards edit `tickets.js` in nearby regions — the markdown-editor recovery in
*Panel Controls That Silently Render Nothing* and the edit-mode messaging in *Safe Auto-Sync*.
Serialise rather than authoring in parallel.
